description: mo:os ontology — aligned with foundation-t158.md. Grammar, not encyclopedia. 36 node types, 18 rewrite categories (WF01-WF18).
invariants: ADD, LINK, MUTATE, UNLINK are the only four rewrites
P(delegate) <= P(principal) — permission inheritance, enforced at rewrite validation time (CI-5)

five_causal_invariants.CI1: Church-Rosser: M_a;M_b = M_b;M_a when affected(M_a) intersect affected(M_b) = empty
five_causal_invariants.CI2: Projection naturality (structure-preserving only): Project(Apply(M,S)) = Apply(M', Project(S)) for projections with declared rewrite correspondence
five_causal_invariants.CI3: Identity stability: forall M forall x: urn(M(x)) = urn(x)
five_causal_invariants.CI4: Log replay determinism: fold(log[0..t]) is deterministic — same log -> same state
five_causal_invariants.CI5: Rewrite category stability: permitted rewrite categories do not change under rewrites — only governance changes the operad

use.node: identity point in graph (not: object, element, vertex)
use.relation: typed connection between nodes (not: binding, edge, wire, association)
use.rewrite: graph transformation operation (not: morphism for the op, update, mutation)
use.rewrite_category: family of allowed rewrites WF01-WF15 (not: named relation, UML association)
use.port: interface point on a node type (not: slot, endpoint)
use.operad: valid composition rules / type registry (not: schema, grammar)
use.property: typed key-value on a node (not: field, payload, attribute)
use.interaction_node: discrete interaction artifact node (not: transition, event, message)

topology_property_boundary.rule: Relations are truth. Properties never duplicate topology.
topology_property_boundary.test: If the information involves two or more nodes, it is a relation (LINK/UNLINK). If it involves only one node's internal state, it is a property (MUTATE).
topology_property_boundary.exception: owner_urn and sender_urn are immutable provenance stamps set at ADD time. They reference another node but are NOT topology.

s2_infrastructure.description: The human principal. Exactly one user per kernel. Superadmin of their own graph.
A running mo:os process. Sovereign — bound to one workstation, owned by one user.
A physical or virtual machine. Hosts kernels, contains compute and storage.
An AI delegate. Defined by properties and capabilities — not by IDE surface. Owned by one user.
s2_infrastructure.note: Capabilities are discovered via WF02 relations to capability nodes — NOT stored as a property on this node (topology-property boundary rule).

s2_infrastructure.description: A bounded interaction context: participants x time interval.
s2_infrastructure.note: Participants are discovered via WF07 relations — NOT stored as a property.

s2_infrastructure.description: A network interface: port + transport. Exposed by kernel, connected-to by agents.
A git repository. Part of the development infrastructure. Hosted on GitHub or local. Contains source code, ontology, or configuration.
A GitHub issue or task. Used as coordination unit between agents. Issues on the project board are the shared task queue. Status syncs with GitHub.

assignee_urn.note: Agent or user assigned. Provenance, not topology.

repo_urn.note: Which repository this issue belongs to. Provenance stamp.

s2_infrastructure.description: A computation substrate. CPU: sequential kernel spine. GPU: concurrent subgraph partitions as hypervector operations.
A persistent storage resource.
A request to promote a local contingent pattern to canonical. Human approval required.
A named bundle of permissions. Attached to delegates via WF02 relations.

builtin_roles.superadmin: all permissions — only principals hold this
builtin_roles.executor: read all, write code nodes and own session
builtin_roles.observer: read all, write own session and ack messages only
builtin_roles.hydrator: read kb, write S0-S2 nodes (ADD only)

s2_infrastructure.description: Scoped permission token. Attached to delegate via WF02 relation. Constrains which rewrite categories the holder can request.

scope.note: list of WF categories this capability grants

s2_infrastructure.description: Program (PRG) — unit of work in mo:os. A branch of the multiway graph that receives runtime. Status lifecycle: planned → active → in_progress → completed | blocked.

t_start.note: Moos-time T-day when PRG runtime began or is scheduled

s2_infrastructure.description: Program node — unit of purposeful work with temporal semantics. Replaces legacy prg_task for new work items. Temporal properties are forward-looking and mutable (plans shift). Dependencies can be known-node (LINK to specific URN) or property-pattern (watcher filter matching ANY node meeting conditions).

owner_urn.note: Provenance stamp — who created this program

scope.note: What this program delivers — mutable because scope evolves

target_t.note: Moos-time T-day target for completion. Mutable: plans shift.

starts_t.note: Moos-time T-day when work begins or is expected to begin

deadline_t.note: Hard deadline in Moos-time. Distinct from target_t (soft target).

completed_t.note: Moos-time T-day when status became completed. Set by MUTATE, not log timestamp.

s2_infrastructure.description: Temporal anchor from Google Calendar. Bridges IRL time to Moos-time. Color-labeled events (purple = PRG-tracked) become graph nodes.
A persistent external source that produces knowledge items. YouTube channel, arxiv category, website RSS, API endpoint. Polled or pushed.

protocol.note: simple label; promote to protocol node via WF14 when capabilities matter

s2_infrastructure.description: A specific piece of content from a source feed. Video, paper, article, email thread. Extracted claims link to domain tags.
An atomic assertion extracted from a knowledge item. The smallest unit of knowledge in the graph.
Classification concept node. Linked to knowledge items and claims. Taxonomy source: arxiv, lcsh, or custom.
Claude or agent session state — kernel snapshot, PRG focus, active connectors. Created at session start, mutated at end.
Presheaf on the rewrite log. Observes rewrites matching a pattern (type, port, URN prefix) and emits observations. Does NOT write — only watches.

match_type_id.note: node type_id to match, or * for any

match_port.note: port name to match on LINK/UNLINK, or empty

s2_infrastructure.description: Natural transformation: observation → proposed rewrite(s). Triggered by a watcher, emits rewrite envelopes for the kernel to validate and apply.

template.note: rewrite envelope template with {{placeholders}} filled from observation

s2_infrastructure.description: Subobject classifier: state predicate that gates a reactor. The reactor only fires if the guard evaluates true against current graph state.

negate.note: if true, guard passes when predicate is FALSE

s1_grammar.description: Network endpoint for a kernel or router. Carries connection details. Linked to kernel via WF05 (exposes).
URN prefix routing rule: maps a URN prefix to a kernel_instance. The router reads these to decide where to forward rewrites.
The cocone/gateway that routes rewrites and queries to kernel instances based on shard_rules. One router can serve multiple kernels.
An S0-S4 classification layer. First-class so the graph can reason about its own strata.

instances.name: authored
instances.description: Human-written seeds, design docs, industry data

instances.name: evaluated
instances.description: Concurrent subgraph eval: hypervector encoding, ranking

instances.name: projected
instances.description: UI, filesystem, API — NEVER ground truth

port_color_compatibility.description: Which source→target port color pairs produce valid relations. Any pair not listed is rejected at validation time.
port_color_compatibility.projection_rule: projection ports are read-only S4 sinks — never source of truth, never form causal relations
port_color_compatibility.semantic_rule: semantic ports (WF15) may compose with any color only when contract_urn is provided

ci2_projection_registry.description: Registry of CI-2 compliant structure-preserving projections. Projections not listed here are lossy — valid for S4 display only, not for authority.

ci2_compliant.definition: All properties of one specific node
ci2_compliant.corresponding_M_prime: MUTATE same field on projected record

ci2_compliant.definition: Agent node + all mutable property values
ci2_compliant.note: Compliant only for MUTATE — not for ADD/UNLINK of unrelated nodes

ci2_compliant.definition: Set of all WF07 relations incident to a session
Set of all WF02 relations from agent to capability nodes
Set of all WF05 relations from kernel to endpoint nodes
Ordered list of all logged rewrites for a kernel

lossy.reason: Aggregate; no M' — many rewrites can produce same delta or cancel
Time-ordered display; insertion doesn't commute with ranking
Many-to-one: same display from different graph states
Filesystem layout != graph topology; multiple S4 views possible
Joins and computed fields have no natural M'

s4_cache_contract.description: Rules governing when and how S4 denormalization caches may exist.

allowed_caches.name: agent_capabilities_cache
allowed_caches.invalidation_trigger: any WF02 LINK or UNLINK on that agent

allowed_caches.name: session_participants_cache
allowed_caches.invalidation_trigger: any WF07 LINK or UNLINK on that session

allowed_caches.name: kernel_endpoints_cache
allowed_caches.invalidation_trigger: any WF05 LINK or UNLINK on that kernel

allowed_caches.name: agent_properties_cache
allowed_caches.invalidation_trigger: any WF02 MUTATE on that agent

forbidden_patterns: capability_urns property on agent node — topology stored as property
participant_urns property on session node — topology stored as property
port_urns property on kernel node — topology stored as property
any S4 cache read by rewrite validator
any S4 cache used to initialize ADD/LINK source

rewrite_categories.name: Ownership
rewrite_categories.description: Principal owns workstation, kernel, or storage.

rewrite_categories.name: Governance
rewrite_categories.description: Principal governs delegate with delegated role and capabilities.

rewrite_categories.name: Connection
rewrite_categories.description: Delegate connects to a kernel endpoint.

rewrite_categories.name: Workflow lifecycle
rewrite_categories.description: Participation, focus, anchoring, and status changes across sessions, PRGs, and calendar events. The workflow-colored WF.

rewrite_categories.name: Substrate binding
rewrite_categories.description: Compute or storage is physically bound to workstation.

rewrite_categories.name: Compute attachment
rewrite_categories.description: Kernel routes operations to compute substrates.

rewrite_categories.name: Persistence
rewrite_categories.description: Kernel's rewrite log persists in a storage resource.

rewrite_categories.name: Sync
rewrite_categories.description: Local storage syncs to/from a remote storage.

rewrite_categories.name: KB provision and hydration
rewrite_categories.description: Knowledge base provision: storage→kernel boot hydration, source_feed→knowledge_item production, knowledge_item→claim extraction, and tagging to domain_tags.

rewrite_categories.name: Promotion
rewrite_categories.description: Governance proposal targets storage/kernel for canonicalization.

rewrite_categories.name: Implementation
rewrite_categories.description: Agent, kernel, or endpoint implements a protocol, language, capability, runtime, or package.

rewrite_categories.name: Semantic (open)
rewrite_categories.description: Open semantic relation. Allowed only with explicit port names AND a contract_schema reference.
rewrite_categories.constraint: No untyped semantic relations — contract_schema required

rewrite_categories.name: Federation
rewrite_categories.description: Routing and connectivity for distributed kernel instances. Router reads shard_rules to route rewrites. Kernels expose endpoints. Shard_rules map URN prefixes to kernel instances.

rewrite_categories.name: Reactive
rewrite_categories.description: Watch/React/Guard pipeline. Watchers observe the rewrite log, trigger reactors when patterns match. Guards gate reactors with state predicates. The firestarter on the carpet.
rewrite_categories.note: Reactive rules are per-kernel — they observe the local log, not remote kernels

rewrite_categories.name: Program composition
rewrite_categories.description: Wires program nodes to their constituent tasks, outputs, sessions, and sub-programs. Temporal dependency DAG. Known-node dependencies use LINK directly; property-pattern dependencies use WF17 watchers that fire when ANY node matching a filter achieves required properties.
